title: External Scope Build And Publish Delivery
summary: Move every Docs Viewer scope to external source, generated, and published ownership and make Build and Publish distinct without deploying document data into site.
content_html:
External Scope Build And Publish Delivery

Requirements

This is the planned second delivery of Scope, Data, And Site Foundations. Its complete result is that every configured Docs Viewer scope has the same application-independent external storage model: canonical source, replaceable generated output, and an accepted consumer-ready published snapshot have separate owners.

Every in-scope root lives beneath $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/ and contains the roles required by that scope. The maximal configured shape is:

<scope>/
  source/
    documents/
    sub-scopes/
    media/
      img/
      svg/
      files/
      html/
      build-source/
        mermaid/
  generated/
    documents/
    search/
    references/
    reports/
    media/
      img/
      svg/
      files/
      html/
  published/
    documents/
    search/
    references/
    reports/
    media/
      img/
      svg/
      files/
      html/

Only types and producers configured for a scope need to materialise. Configured directories remain present when empty: their emptiness is useful evidence that the role exists and currently contains no files rather than evidence that setup was forgotten. Source contains canonical Markdown and all Docs Viewer-managed source media. A directly managed image, SVG, file, or HTML object is authoritative beneath its source type; a producer input such as Mermaid is authoritative beneath source/media/build-source/. A retained original elsewhere in Projects remains optional provenance rather than a second Docs Viewer authority.

Build writes replaceable document, Search, reference, report, and media products only to generated output. Direct ready media may be copied unchanged, while producer media may derive different bytes such as Mermaid source becoming SVG. Generated media is the exact consumer-ready media set required by the generated document snapshot; an unreferenced source-media object may therefore remain in source without entering generated output. Publish promotes the complete accepted document-and-media set from generated output into published output. Published media likewise contains the exact set required by the accepted published documents. Published output is consumer-neutral: Manage, Swift, or another application can read it without requiring source, generated output, the repository, site/, a local web server, GitHub Pages, or dotlineform.com.

The current $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/docs-viewer/media/<scope>/ workspace is the active pre-migration private managed-media authority. Stage 2 inventories and byte-verifies it, moves its ready media, registered build sources, and source evidence into the owning scope's source/media/ branch, and retires the separate top-level docs-viewer/media/ workspace after every scope has passed its cutover gate. Existing inactive media directories inside scope roots are migration residue, not an alternative authority. The cutover introduces no alias, fallback read, dual write, or second canonical media location.

Storage provider and public exposure are independent. Scope-root location owns where source, generated, and published data live; public-projection configuration owns whether a later Deploy Repo operation is available. The current local, local_external, and public scope types must no longer infer storage provider, publishability, or public exposure.

The processing Docs Viewer scope participates exactly like the other scopes. The separate processing/ Java/Processing code project, its dependencies, and its future build, test, and release lifecycle remain outside this delivery.

The migration is deliberately manual and recoverable. The final clean Git commit containing repository-owned scope source is the recovery snapshot. The user creates the external folders and copies canonical source and source media; implementation verifies the copied relative paths and bytes before switching configuration. No migration UI, recurring snapshot system, version-history feature, dual reader, compatibility alias, or fallback to the repository copy is introduced. Repository copies are removed only after the external source and new Build and Publish paths have been accepted.

Stage 2 does not write document, Search, or media data into site/. The current tracked Analysis public snapshot remains stable until Stage 3 introduces Deploy Repo. Scope Publish must not call the current Analysis site-projection operation implicitly. This delivery does not implement Deploy Repo, repository commit or push, Deploy Public, a GitHub Pages change, Swift code, Catalogue migration, or the processing/ project lifecycle.

Process

The normal lifecycle after this delivery is:

external canonical source
  -> Build
external generated output
  -> working review in Manage
  -> Publish
external accepted published snapshot
  -> published review in Manage
  -> Swift or another direct consumer

tracked site document projection
  -> unchanged during Stage 2

Identical bytes in more than one lifecycle layer are intentional snapshot isolation rather than duplicate authority. Each layer remains independently inspectable and no symlink, hard link, fallback, or implicit cross-layer read is part of the contract. A same-filename media replacement demonstrates the state boundary:

Replace source/media/img/image.jpg
  source: new
  generated: old
  published: old

Run Build
  source: new
  generated: new
  published: old

Run Publish
  source: new
  generated: new
  published: new

The bytes need not always match: a registered producer can transform source media during Build, and later media capabilities may sanitize, resize, convert, or create variants without changing the three ownership roles.

Build and Publish reconcile their owned output files in place rather than replacing or renaming whole directory trees. Each operation computes the exact target file manifest, removes its previous completion record, deletes stale owned files, writes new and changed files, leaves byte-identical files untouched, verifies the resulting file set and bytes, and writes the new completion record last. Configured directories are created when missing and retained when empty; unexpected directories are reported for review rather than pruned merely because they contain no files.

No staging-tree swap, backup-directory rename, rollback copy, symlink, or other filesystem indirection is introduced. A failed operation may leave its output incomplete; the missing completion record makes that state explicit, source remains intact, and the operator fixes the cause and reruns the same Build or Publish until the reconciliation succeeds. This simple convergent workflow deliberately favours transparent files and low iCloud churn over transactional directory replacement.

The current directories named published/ contain working builder output, not an accepted publication layer. Readiness records them as the pre-cutover generated baseline. The new Build writes generated/; the first genuine Publish previews and reconciles published/ to the accepted snapshot. Existing bytes are never declared accepted merely because they already occupy that directory.

Publish is a scope-wide preview and apply operation. Preview is write-free and identifies the generated revision, target published revision, included and excluded documents, and planned additions, changes, and removals. Apply revalidates the preview, applies publishable: false to the complete collection, prepares consumer-neutral payloads, and reconciles the confined published files in place to the exact accepted manifest. It does not rebuild, mutate canonical source, rename the published tree, create a rollback snapshot, transfer to site or R2 deployment destinations, commit, push, or release GitHub Pages.

Manage distinguishes generated and published reads explicitly. Generated is the normal working view after Build; Published is the last accepted snapshot. A missing or unavailable published snapshot is reported as its own state and never falls back to generated. Public routes continue to read the existing tracked site/ snapshot throughout this delivery.

Migration activates the common model on an already-external private scope first, then uses the processing Docs Viewer scope as the first repository-backed cutover, followed by Studio and Analysis last. The existing external Notes, Dotlineform, and App scopes retain their canonical source locations while gaining the generated/published distinction. All required external folders may be prepared in advance, but each activation is verified before the next scope becomes authoritative.

Deliverables

New And Changed Files

Path or family Change
docs-viewer/config/scopes/docs_scopes.json and scope-schema validation Give every configured scope one external scope root, derive source/generated/published document and media roles beneath it, retire the separate top-level media workspace, and separate storage provider from public exposure and publishability.
docs-viewer/services/docs_scope_config.py, docs_scope_manifest.py, and artifact-location helpers Resolve and validate source, generated, and published locations through one provider-neutral boundary; reject missing, overlapping, unsafe, or capability-incomplete roots without manufacturing partial scopes.
docs-viewer/build/build_docs.py, build_search.py, and docs_builder/ Write the working document, Search, reference, report, directly copied media, and derived-media products to external generated output rather than the current published/ and separate managed-media paths.
Docs watcher, write/rebuild, generated-read, package, import/export, report, and scope-lifecycle services Read canonical source and generated output through the configured locations and preserve exact scope/sub-scope identity without repository-path assumptions or compatibility fallbacks.
Scope Publish preview/apply service and focused tests Add one provider-neutral whole-scope operation that reconciles the confined published files in place to the exact accepted generated document-and-media manifest, preserves configured empty directories, owns publishability, and never writes deployment destinations.
Docs Viewer management client, controls, providers, and route configuration Expose Build and Publish for every available scope and let Manage read generated or published output explicitly without granting public-site deployment authority.
Current Analysis site-projection owner Remove it from scope Publish composition while retaining the bounded existing deployment seam for Stage 3; do not silently invoke it, rename it as Publish, or broaden the runtime site-code manifest.
Repository scope workspaces and external scope roots After verified activation, remove inactive repository-owned source, old working-output trees, inactive media residue, and the retired top-level external media workspace; leave processing/ code untouched.
Scope/build/publish/runtime tests and durable Docs Viewer documentation Protect exact location roles, byte-confined migration, generated/published isolation, rerunnable in-place reconciliation, completion-record validity, configured empty directories, unavailable-root behavior, public-site non-mutation, and the final operator workflow.

No runtime code projection, public route shell, public-site document projection, R2 deployment, Catalogue data, repository commit/push, GitHub Action, or Processing project code enters this delivery.

Processes To Be Run

  • Record the clean recovery commit and inventory the current scope roots, separate managed-media workspace, registered build sources, source evidence, working output, public-site projections, and provider boundaries before migration.
  • Let the user create the external scope trees and copy canonical source and source media; verify exact relative paths and bytes before any configured cutover.
  • Introduce the one-root external source/generated/published document-and-media model without aliases, fallback reads, automatic root creation, or duplicated authority.
  • Rebuild every configured scope into external generated output and compare the relevant payload contracts with the pre-cutover working baseline.
  • Exercise Manage against generated output for existing external scopes, then Processing, Studio, and Analysis in the accepted order.
  • Preview and apply the first external published snapshot for every scope, confirming publishability, the exact corresponding media set, in-place stale-file removal, unchanged-file preservation, completion-record-last behavior, configured empty directories, consumer-neutral bytes, and generated/published isolation.
  • Exercise Manage's explicit generated and published views and confirm that unavailable or missing output is reported without cross-layer fallback.
  • Confirm that tracked site/, the current public Analysis route, R2 objects, runtime projection, GitHub Pages workflow, and processing/ code project remain unchanged.
  • Remove inactive repository scope source, old working outputs, inactive scope-media residue, and finally the separate external media workspace only after external source, Build, Publish, and recovery evidence are accepted.
  • Update the durable storage, Build, Publish, source-tree, setup, and recovery documentation owners named by readiness.

Delivery Steps

2.0 — Readiness

  • [ ] Confirm the complete configured scope set, current scope roots, separate managed-media namespaces, registered build sources, inactive media residue, working/public locations, provider capabilities, direct consumers, and every place where scope type currently implies storage, publishability, or exposure.
  • [ ] Record the final clean Git recovery commit and the exact canonical document, ready-media, build-source, and source-evidence inventory that the user will copy; confirm the one-root external destination layout and byte-verification method without creating a migration subsystem.
  • [ ] Confirm the migration order: an existing external private scope, the Processing Docs Viewer scope, Studio, and Analysis last; keep the processing/ code project outside the blast radius.
  • [ ] Confirm the interim release boundary: Stage 2 Publish changes only external published snapshots, while the tracked public Analysis snapshot remains unchanged until Stage 3 Deploy Repo.
  • [ ] Set a proportional verification budget for scope configuration, Build output ownership, generated/published reads, whole-scope Publish, migration cleanup, unavailable external roots, and public-site non-mutation.

Gate: present the confirmed location and consumer boundary, manual-copy and recovery plan, migration order, temporary Analysis release limitation, credible blast radius, and any necessary change to these deliverables before editing configuration or code.

2.1 — External Scope And Generated Cutover

  • [ ] Verify the user's external document, ready-media, build-source, and source-evidence copies against the recorded inventory before making them authoritative.
  • [ ] Move every configured scope to the common one-root external location model and make source, generated, published, and public projection distinct configuration roles; retire the top-level media-workspace contract.
  • [ ] Cut Build, Search, media production, watcher, rebuild, generated reads, and affected service consumers over to external generated output with no repository, old media-workspace, or published/ fallback.
  • [ ] Activate and verify scopes in the accepted order, preserving exact parent/sub-scope identity and reporting unavailable roots without creating partial workspaces.

Gate: every configured scope reads canonical external document and media source from its one scope root and produces an exact replaceable generated document-and-media snapshot; Manage works against generated data; old repository and media-workspace sources are inactive but retained for recovery; tracked site/ is unchanged.

2.2 — Scope Publish And Published Review

  • [ ] Implement write-free preview and confirmed whole-scope Publish from generated output to the external published snapshot for every scope using rerunnable in-place file reconciliation rather than a directory swap or rollback tree.
  • [ ] Make Publish own complete document eligibility: publishable: false remains visible in generated working output and is absent with its owned descendants from published output.
  • [ ] Prepare consumer-neutral published documents, Search, references, reports, and the exact media required by those documents; delete stale files, leave byte-identical files untouched, preserve configured empty directories, verify the resulting manifest, and write the completion record last without destination-specific site/R2 transfer or another consumer-specific filter.
  • [ ] Let Manage select and clearly identify generated versus published reads; reject missing, unavailable, or stale published state without falling back to generated.
  • [ ] Remove the current Analysis site projection from Publish composition while leaving the tracked public snapshot and Stage 3 deployment seam unchanged.

Gate: each scope has an independently reviewable accepted document-and-media snapshot, every published consumer sees the same document and media set, a failed reconciliation is visibly incomplete and succeeds when rerun, configured empty directories remain, Publish writes no deployment destination, and Analysis public bytes remain unchanged.

2.3 — Migration Cleanup And Development Integration

  • [ ] Update source writes, imports, packages, exports, scope/sub-scope lifecycle, reports, local links, capabilities, and path reporting to use the common external ownership model without scope-type or repository-path assumptions.
  • [ ] Remove inactive repository source, old working-output trees, and inactive media residue only after the external source, generated, and published snapshots for that scope have passed their gates; remove the separate top-level media workspace only after every scope has passed; retain the recorded Git commit as the recovery boundary.
  • [ ] Record the manual setup, Build, Publish, generated/published review, unavailable-root, and recovery workflow in repository instructions and durable documentation.
  • [ ] Confirm that the repository contains code/config and the tracked site snapshot, not canonical scope source, replaceable generated output, or external accepted published output, and that no active Docs Viewer path remains beneath the retired top-level media workspace.

Gate: the normal local workflow uses external source/generated/published ownership end to end, no startup or fallback recreates retired repository scope data, and a fresh Codex task receives the correct handoff automatically.

2.4 — Code Review

  • [ ] Review the bounded configuration, providers, builders, watcher, services, browser composition, migration removals, tests, documentation, external generated/published outputs, and repository diff for duplicate owners, compatibility residue, unsafe or non-convergent file reconciliation, directory-swap or rollback-tree machinery, provider leakage, hidden repository reads, accidental site/R2 writes, and Processing project crossover.
  • [ ] Resolve findings and rerun only the evidence affected by review changes.

Gate: present the reviewed change set, external and repository deltas, remaining omissions, and focused evidence for approval before closeout.

2.5 — Closeout

  • [ ] Confirm that every configured Docs Viewer scope has one external canonical source, replaceable generated output, and accepted published snapshot while the tracked public site and Processing project lifecycle remain unchanged.
  • [ ] Update durable owners and record only genuine Stage 3 prerequisites discovered during implementation; do not extend this delivery into Deploy Repo, commit/push, or Deploy Public.
  • [ ] Point the parent feature clearly to the next Document Deployment And Pages Release delivery and recommend whether this delivery should be retained for review or retired after its stable conclusions have moved.

Gate: close only after the user accepts the shipped outcome and explicitly authorizes the feature to proceed to Stage 3 rather than extending Stage 2.
